review_notes: I read the entire 132-line target and the main dependencies it builds on: CoulombTransport/CompactSeparation.lean (exists_uniform_compact_separation), CoulombTransport/BranchCoupling.lean (branchMarginal, branchCoupling, ae_branchCoupling), CoulombTransport/CoulombEstimates.lean (Separated, lintegral_coulombCost_lt_top_of_ae_separated), and Model.lean for E3/Triple. The only definition in the file is `components`, which is a problem-specific named family (the central set K plus its four images H i '' K) and is definitionally built from Mathlib's `Fin.cases`/`Fin.cons` API. It is a named specialization for a specific construction, not an independent competing version of a Mathlib concept; there is no duplicate Mathlib API for 'central set and four transported copies', and replacing it with `Fin.cons K (fun i => H i '' K)` would only change the implementation and would not remove any substantive concept. I searched Mathlib for related notions (`Metric.IsSeparated`, `Metric.AreSeparated`, `SeparatedNhds`, `PairwiseDisjoint`, the Fin tuple API) and found no existing statement of the same specific concept covered by this file. The remaining declarations (`compact_components`, `measurableSet_separated`, `exists_ae_separated_branchCoupling`, `ae_mem_branchMarginal_components`, `compact_support_and_separation`, `disjoint_components_mono`, `finite_cost_branchCoupling`) are theorems/lemmas, and under the rubric standalone theorem duplication and proof shortening are out of scope; `measurableSet_separated` in particular is a proof-level measurability fact about the local `CoulombEstimates.Separated` predicate, not a new definition competing with Mathlib. I did not execute Lean, so any proposed replacement would be untested; no replacement is proposed.
